justification: Six forms of one 2nd-declension masculine paradigm (-us, -i, -orum, -is, -os, vocative -e), 101 tokens in the Clementine Vulgate. Lewis & Short (1879, public domain) s.v. Pharisaeus, i, m. Not in DICTLINE at the pinned commit.

Four plural forms of a 2nd-declension masculine paradigm, 14 tokens in the Clementine Vulgate. Lewis & Short (1879) heads it in the plural, Sadducaei, orum, m.; the singular heading here follows pharisaeus and is not itself attested in the Vulgate. Not in DICTLINE.

One form, always lower-case, 30 tokens in four books of the Clementine Vulgate, in several constructions: a Hebrew word the Vulgate leaves undeclined. Filed undeclined and neuter as DICTLINE files ephod and manna (the gender is not evidenced). Not in Lewis & Short or DICTLINE.
One form, lower-case, 4 tokens in two books of the Clementine Vulgate: a Hebrew word left undeclined. Filed as setim is. Not in Lewis & Short or DICTLINE.
Written lower-case 6 times, all in Isaiah, as a common noun (the capitalised Carmel is the mountain, a name). One form: left undeclined, filed as setim is. Not in Lewis & Short or DICTLINE.
DICTLINE has basis (N 3 9, Greek accusatives -in/-on/-a) but not the Latin accusatives the Vulgate uses: basim 10, basem 1. Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. basis: accusative usually basim, but basem.

prophetidem 2 in the Clementine Vulgate, accusative of a 3rd-declension -is, -idis noun. Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. prophetis, idis, f., a prophetess (citing the Vulgate). Limited to the attested form: prophetis itself is also propheta's dative and ablative plural.

The Vulgate spells DICTLINE's empticius with -titius (emptitius 2, emptitii 1), and no WORDS trick turns ti into ci. Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. empticius: '(emt-) or -titius'. The forms are read as DICTLINE's lemma.

sardonycho 1 in the Clementine Vulgate (Job), a 1st/2nd-declension adjective beside a noun. Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. sardonyx: 'Hence, adj.', of sardonyx, citing this verse (spelled sardonichus there; the Vulgate's spelling is kept). DICTLINE has only the noun sardonyx.
mygale 1 in the Clementine Vulgate (Leviticus). Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. mygale, es, f. (Greek 1st declension). Not in DICTLINE.
DICTLINE has psaltes (N 1 7, accusative -en or -am) but not the accusative -em the Vulgate uses once, with the nominative psaltes in the next clause. Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. psaltes, ae, m.
myro 1 in the Clementine Vulgate (Judith), an ablative. Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. myron or myrum, i, n., an ointment (eccl. Lat.). Not in DICTLINE (which has myrrha, a different word).
The Vulgate spells DICTLINE's smegma with i (smigmata 1, Daniel); no WORDS trick turns i into e. Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. smegma: '(smigma and zmegma)'. Read as DICTLINE's lemma.
querulosi 1 in the Clementine Vulgate (Jude). Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. querulosus, a, um, citing this verse. Not in DICTLINE (which has querulus).
nerviceis 1 in the Clementine Vulgate (Judges). Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. nerviceus, a, um, made of sinews, citing this verse. Not in DICTLINE.

onustati 1 in the Clementine Vulgate (Judith), a perfect passive participle. Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. onusto, are, 1, v. a., 'only late Lat. and in Part. pass.', citing this verse. No perfect active is attested, so none is given (zzz). DICTLINE has only the adjective onustus.

The Vulgate spells DICTLINE's pirus with y (pyrorum 4); WORDS's y/i trick applies only to a first letter. Lewis & Short (1879): 'pyrum and pyrus, v. pirum and pirus'. Read as DICTLINE's lemma; the pear (pirum) is given as well, as WORDS gives both for pirorum.
As house:pyrus, for DICTLINE's pirum (the fruit).
quaesumus 2 in the Clementine Vulgate: the 1st plural of quaeso (an old form of quaero, Lewis & Short 1879), which DICTLINE lists but whose regular endings give quaesimus.

ruituri 1 in the Clementine Vulgate (Ezekiel), the future active participle of ruo. Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. ruo: 'ruiturus, a, um' (Ovid, Lucan, Martial, Pliny). DICTLINE's fourth stem (rut-) gives only ruturus.

of: sancio, sancire, sanxi, sanctus  V (4th) TRANS
justification: sancitum 1 in the Clementine Vulgate (Hebrews). Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. sancio: 'part. perf. sancitum' (Lucretius). DICTLINE's fourth stem gives only sanctum.

of: circumlino, circumlinere, circumlevi, circumlitus  V (3rd) TRANS
justification: circumlinisti 1 in the Clementine Vulgate (Ezekiel). Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. circumlino: 'perf. late Lat. circumlinisti', citing this verse. DICTLINE's perfect stem is circumlev-.
plexueris 1 in the Clementine Vulgate (Judges). Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. plecto (to plait): perfect 'xi and xui'. DICTLINE's perfect stem is plex- only.

fasciaretur 1 in the Clementine Vulgate (Ezekiel). Lewis & Short (1879) s.v. fascio, 'no perf., atum, 1, v. a.', citing this verse ('Pass., Vulg. Ezech.'). No perfect is given (zzz). DICTLINE has only the noun fascia.
